chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Hamzih ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Basam narrated that Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Ibrahim al-Sa'di narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah al-Yamani narrated that Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Muqri narrated that Hammad ibn Amr al-Naseebi, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stood among us as a preacher and said at the end of his sermon: 'God, the Exalted, has gathered for us ten characteristics which He did not gather for anyone before us, nor will they be in anyone other than us: Among us are wisdom, forbearance, knowledge, prophethood, generosity, bravery, moderation, honesty, purity, and modesty. We are the word of piety, the path of guidance, the highest example, the great proof, the firm bond, and the strong rope. We are those for whom God commanded love. So what follows the truth except deviation? How then will you be turned away?'

key_terms.بِالْمَوَدَّةِ: Love (specifically divine command to love them)

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics God gathered in the Prophet and his Household according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) enumerates ten exclusive virtues—such as wisdom, knowledge, and purity—united in him and the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing their unique spiritual authority. He identifies them as the 'firmest handhold' (Al-Wurqa al-Mutina) and asserts that God commanded love for them, linking this divine mandate to the concept of *Mawadda* in Surah Ash-Shura. This narration underscores the Shia belief that the Ahl al-Bayt are the infallible guides and the ultimate embodiment of divine guidance, making love for them a prerequisite for true faith.
